sentence: The menu is ___ the top of the page.
explanation: We say 'at the top' and 'at the bottom' of a page.

sentence: The logo is ___ the left.
explanation: We say 'on the left' and 'on the right'.

sentence: The heading is in the ___ of the page.
explanation: After 'the', you need a noun: the centre. 'Central' is an adjective.

sentence: Visitors can ___ down to see more projects.
explanation: After 'can', use the base verb: can scroll.

sentence: The gallery ___ twelve photos.
explanation: 'The gallery' is singular, so add -s: shows.

sentence: There ___ three buttons under the heading.
explanation: 'Three buttons' is plural, so 'there are'. Don't use 'have' here.

sentence: The text is easy ___ because the font is large.
explanation: easy + to + base verb: easy to read.

sentence: This website has ___ about the school's sports clubs.
explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: no -s and no 'a' or 'an'.

sentence: Maya's portfolio has ___ simple layout.
explanation: 'Layout' is countable, so it needs 'a'. Use 'a' before a consonant sound: a simple layout.

sentence: Leo's website has ___ orange background.
explanation: Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an orange background.

sentence: The images are too ___ together, so the page looks busy.
explanation: 'Close together' means near each other. 'Closed' means not open.

sentence: The layout is ___, so visitors don't know where to click.
explanation: Things that cause confusion are 'confusing'. People feel 'confused'.

sentence: The big photo ___ visitors notice the products.
explanation: 'The big photo' is singular: helps. Then help + person + base verb: helps visitors notice.

sentence: The bright colours make the site ___ fun.
explanation: make + something + base verb (no 'to', no -s): make the site feel.

sentence: The pictures are arranged in rows and ___.
explanation: Rows and columns: both plural. A grid is made of rows and columns.

sentence: Last week, I ___ a dark blue background for my site.
explanation: 'Last week' needs the past simple. 'Choose' is irregular: chose.

sentence: The pages are well ___, so it is easy to find things.
explanation: be + well + past participle: well organised.

sentence: Click this button ___ download the poster.
explanation: Use 'to' + verb to say why you do something.

sentence: The bold font ___ the most important words.
explanation: 'The bold font' is singular, so the verb needs -s. 'Emphasis' is a noun.

sentence: The yellow button stands ___ against the dark background.
explanation: 'Stand out' means be more noticeable than the things around it.

sentence: The playful images might appeal ___ young children.
explanation: We say 'appeal to' someone.

sentence: The website is aimed ___ teenagers who like gaming.
explanation: A website is 'aimed at' its target audience.

sentence: The colours are used ___ across every page.
explanation: To describe how something is done (are used), use an adverb: consistently.

sentence: There is a lot of ___ around the text, so the page feels calm.
explanation: 'Whitespace' is uncountable: no -s. Clutter would make the page feel busy, not calm.

sentence: The dark colours create ___ serious mood.
explanation: 'Mood' is countable: a serious mood. Use 'a' before a consonant sound.

sentence: The new homepage hero is ___ effective than the old one.
explanation: To compare two things, use 'more' + adjective + 'than'.

sentence: The call to action ___ visitors to contact Maya.
explanation: 'The call to action' is singular: encourages. Then encourage + person + to + verb.

sentence: Users find the menu easily because it follows a familiar ___.
explanation: After 'a familiar', you need a singular noun: convention.

sentence: One piece of ___ is the large red button.
explanation: 'Evidence' is uncountable: no -s. 'Evident' is an adjective.

sentence: The site looks ___ because every element lines up.
explanation: After 'looks', use an adjective: structured.

sentence: With responsive design, the layout ___ to fit different screens.
explanation: 'The layout' is singular, so add -s: changes.

sentence: The left side is cluttered, ___ the right side is spacious.
explanation: 'Whereas' shows a contrast between two things.

sentence: The aim of the CTA is to make visitors ___ the form.
explanation: make + person + base verb (no 'to'): make visitors submit.

sentence: Typography ___ an important part of a website's visual identity.
explanation: 'Typography' is uncountable, so it takes a singular verb: is.

sentence: Compared ___ the first design, the second one is more welcoming.
explanation: We say 'compared with' (or 'compared to'). Use 'than' only after a comparative, e.g. 'more welcoming than'.

sentence: Last year, the designer ___ legibility by using a larger sans-serif font.
explanation: 'Last year' needs the past simple: improved.

sentence: Good accessibility means ___ users can navigate the site.
explanation: 'Every' is followed by a singular noun (every user). With a plural noun, use 'all': all users.

sentence: The site has very ___ clutter, so the focal point is clear.
explanation: 'Clutter' is uncountable, so use 'little', not 'few'.

sentence: A design brief should explain the purpose, the audience and the ___.
explanation: You need a plural noun here. Never use an apostrophe to make a plural.

sentence: Last lesson, we ___ the site on three different phones.
explanation: 'Last lesson' needs the past simple: tested.

sentence: The symmetrical layout ___ a sense of balance.
explanation: 'The symmetrical layout' is singular, so the verb needs -s: creates.

sentence: If the images were compressed, the page ___ faster.
explanation: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb.

sentence: The site's credibility ___ by the spelling mistakes in the About section.
explanation: Passive: is + past participle. The mistakes reduce the credibility.

sentence: This is the third ___ of the homepage.
explanation: After 'the third', you need a noun: iteration.

sentence: The designer's ___ was to make the site feel approachable.
explanation: After 'the designer's', you need a noun: intention.

sentence: An intuitive menu lets visitors ___ what they need quickly.
explanation: let + person + base verb (no 'to'): lets visitors find.

sentence: The hover state makes it clear ___ the image is a link.
explanation: it is clear + that + a full sentence.

sentence: Yesterday, the AI tool ___ three different layouts from my prompt.
explanation: 'Yesterday' needs the past simple: generated. 'Generation' is a noun.

sentence: Engagement ___ higher since the site added a quiz.
explanation: With 'since', use the present perfect: has been.

sentence: The more ___ the layout is, the easier the site is to use.
explanation: The word describes the layout (after 'is'), so use an adjective: intuitive.

sentence: My website ___ three pages: Home, About and Contact.
explanation: 'My website' is singular, so use 'has'.

sentence: The photos ___ very bright and colourful.
explanation: 'The photos' is plural, so use 'are'.

sentence: There ___ a big button below the heading.
explanation: 'A big button' is singular, so use 'there is'.

sentence: Visitors can find the contact form ___ the bottom of the page.
explanation: We say 'at the bottom' and 'at the top' of a page.

sentence: The heading is ___ the image.
explanation: 'Above' means higher than. 'On top' needs 'of': on top of.

sentence: The logo is ___ the menu.
explanation: 'Beside' means next to. 'Besides' means 'as well as'.

sentence: Leo's homepage has ___ animation of a robot.
explanation: Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an animation.

sentence: I made ___ website about my favourite band.
explanation: 'Website' is countable, so it needs 'a'. 'W' is a consonant sound.

sentence: The text is ___ to read because the font is very small.
explanation: After 'is', use an adjective: difficult. 'Difficulty' is a noun.

sentence: The page looks very ___.
explanation: After 'looks very', use an adjective: organised.

sentence: The site is easy to use and very ___.
explanation: After 'very', use an adjective: friendly.

sentence: Yesterday, I ___ a new photo to my gallery.
explanation: 'Yesterday' needs the past simple: added.

sentence: Last week, our class ___ websites about our hobbies.
explanation: 'Make' is irregular: the past simple is 'made'.

sentence: Now the site ___ much faster than before.
explanation: 'The site' is singular, so add -s: loads.

sentence: There are many ___ in Maya's gallery.
explanation: After 'many', use a plural noun. 'Photo' just adds -s: photos.

sentence: The website gives lots of useful ___.
explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: no -s and no 'an'.

sentence: The bakery website has a lot of ___ of cakes.
explanation: After 'a lot of', use a plural noun you can count: pictures.

sentence: The new heading is ___ than the old one.
explanation: Short adjectives add -er: bigger than. 'Biggest' is for the top of a group.

sentence: This is the ___ page on the whole website.
explanation: To say 'number one in a group', short adjectives add -est: the longest.

sentence: Leo's site is ___ colourful than Maya's.
explanation: Comparing two things with a long adjective: more colourful than.

sentence: The page is busy, ___ it is hard to find the menu.
explanation: 'So' introduces the result: the page is busy, so it is hard to find things.

sentence: I like the colours, ___ the font is too small.
explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast: something good, then something bad.

sentence: The site feels friendly ___ it uses bright colours.
explanation: 'Because' gives the reason.

sentence: Tap the arrow ___ see the next photo.
explanation: Use 'to' + verb to say why you do something.

sentence: The large photo makes visitors ___ the products.
explanation: make + person + base verb (no 'to'): makes visitors notice.

sentence: The button helps visitors ___ the contact page.
explanation: help + person + base verb: helps visitors find.

sentence: Visitors can ___ videos on the homepage.
explanation: After 'can', use the base verb: can watch.

sentence: You should not ___ too many colours.
explanation: After 'should not', use the base verb: use.

sentence: Maya ___ photos of nature.
explanation: 'Maya' is one person, so add -s: takes.

sentence: The menu ___ have a link to the Contact page.
explanation: 'The menu' is singular: doesn't + base verb.

sentence: ___ the colours bright enough?
explanation: 'The colours' is plural: Are the colours …?

sentence: My favourite part of the site ___ the gallery.
explanation: The subject is 'my favourite part' (singular): is.

sentence: When you click the button, a new page ___.
explanation: 'A new page' is singular, so add -s: opens.

sentence: The colour palette ___ of three shades of blue.
explanation: 'The colour palette' is singular: consists of.

sentence: The playful font is suitable ___ a children's website.
explanation: We say 'suitable for' something.

sentence: The designer focused ___ the photos rather than the text.
explanation: We say 'focus on' something.

sentence: Whitespace draws attention ___ the call to action.
explanation: We say 'draw attention to' something.

sentence: This website is very different ___ Leo's.
explanation: We say 'different from'.

sentence: The homepage hero is the first thing visitors see, so it ___ make a strong impression.
explanation: Modal verbs like 'should' and 'must' are followed by the base verb, with no 'to'.

sentence: The tone of the site ___ informal and friendly.
explanation: The subject is 'the tone' (singular), not 'the site': is.

sentence: Each of the pages ___ the same header.
explanation: 'Each of' is followed by a singular verb: each of the pages has.

sentence: The images on the homepage ___ the site feel energetic.
explanation: The subject is 'the images' (plural), not 'the homepage': make.

sentence: Using too many fonts ___ a site look cluttered.
explanation: An -ing subject (Using too many fonts) is singular: makes.

sentence: The site has a ___ layout, with everything lined up neatly.
explanation: Before a noun (layout), use an adjective: a structured layout.

sentence: The bold red button creates a sense of ___.
explanation: After 'a sense of', use a noun: urgency.

sentence: The design is simple but ___.
explanation: After 'is … but', use another adjective: effective.

sentence: The text is ___ readable, even on a small phone.
explanation: Before an adjective (readable), use an adverb: easily readable.

sentence: The site is ___ to young people because of its bright colours.
explanation: After 'is', use an adjective: appealing.

sentence: There ___ a lot of whitespace around the logo.
explanation: 'Whitespace' is uncountable, so use 'there is'.

sentence: The menu has too ___ options, so it feels cluttered.
explanation: Use 'many' with plural nouns you can count: too many options.

sentence: There is too ___ text on the homepage.
explanation: 'Text' is uncountable here, so use 'much': too much text.

sentence: The second version is ___ more spacious than the first.
explanation: To make a comparative stronger, use 'much': much more spacious.

sentence: The new font is ___ readable as the old one.
explanation: To say two things are equal: as + adjective + as.

sentence: This is the ___ effective page on the site.
explanation: 'The most' + long adjective means number one in a group.

sentence: The site looks professional. ___, the font is quite hard to read.
explanation: 'However,' starts a new sentence that contrasts with the one before.

sentence: ___ the site is colourful, it still looks professional.
explanation: 'Although' + a full clause. 'Despite' needs a noun or -ing form.

sentence: The layout is clear. ___, the colours are calm and consistent.
explanation: 'In addition,' adds another point at the start of a new sentence.

sentence: Visitors can contact Maya ___ filling in the form.
explanation: Use 'by' + -ing to say how you do something.

sentence: The designer avoided ___ too many fonts.
explanation: 'Avoid' is followed by the -ing form: avoided using.

sentence: The call to action encourages visitors ___ in touch.
explanation: encourage + person + to + verb: encourages visitors to get in touch.

sentence: The design ___ by a professional photographer's website.
explanation: Passive: was + past participle. The website inspired the design.

sentence: All the images ___ in a neat grid.
explanation: Passive: are + past participle (displayed).

sentence: The site was designed for people ___ love hiking.
explanation: Use 'who' for people.

sentence: Maya chose a colour palette ___ reflects her calm personality.
explanation: Use 'that' (or 'which') for things. 'Who' is for people.

sentence: Last term, we ___ three different homepage designs.
explanation: 'Last term' needs the past simple: compared.

sentence: I ___ the colour palette twice since the first draft.
explanation: With 'since', use the present perfect. 'I' takes 'have': I have changed.

sentence: Usability would improve ___ the menu were moved to the top.
explanation: Second conditional: would + base verb … if + past. 'Unless' gives the opposite meaning.

sentence: If the designer ___ fewer fonts, the site would look more cohesive.
explanation: Second conditional: If + past simple (used), would + base verb. Don't put 'would' after 'if'.

sentence: If visitors can't find the menu, they ___ leave the site.
explanation: First conditional (a real possibility): If + present, will + base verb.

sentence: The images ___ before the site was published.
explanation: Passive past perfect: had been + past participle. The images didn't compress anything themselves.

sentence: Alt text ___ to every image to improve accessibility.
explanation: Passive with a modal: should be + past participle (added).

sentence: The final design ___ against the brief by the whole class.
explanation: Passive: was + past participle. The class evaluated the design.

sentence: The site, ___ was designed by a Year 8 student, won a prize.
explanation: After a comma, use 'which' for things. 'That' can't follow a comma.

sentence: Maya, ___ portfolio we analysed, is a wildlife photographer.
explanation: 'Whose' shows possession (her portfolio). 'Who's' means 'who is'.

sentence: The section ___ the prices are listed is hard to find.
explanation: Use 'where' for a place, including a place on a page.

sentence: The ___ of a clear focal point makes the page feel confusing.
explanation: After 'the', you need a noun: the absence of.

sentence: The ___ of the menu improves usability.
explanation: After 'the', you need a noun: the simplification of.

sentence: Strong contrast improves ___ for users with poor eyesight.
explanation: After 'improves', you need a noun: accessibility.

sentence: The site is not very ___, because it is hard to use without instructions.
explanation: After 'is not very', use an adjective: intuitive.

sentence: The designer's choices are ___ justified with evidence.
explanation: Before a past participle (justified), use an adverb: clearly.

sentence: A ___ layout can make a portfolio more memorable.
explanation: Before a noun (layout), use an adjective: distinctive.

sentence: Overall, the site ___ the requirements of the brief.
explanation: 'The site' is singular, so add -s: meets.

sentence: Every page on the site ___ a clear heading.
explanation: 'Every' is followed by a singular verb: every page has.

sentence: The number of images on the homepage ___ the loading time.
explanation: 'The number of' is singular: increases. ('A number of' would be plural.)

sentence: One of the main strengths of the site ___ its navigation.
explanation: The subject is 'one' (singular), not 'strengths': is.

sentence: The site ___ more engaging since the quiz was added.
explanation: With 'since', use the present perfect: has + past participle (become).

sentence: By the time we tested the site, we ___ the images.
explanation: For an action before another past action, use the past perfect: had compressed.

sentence: The designer ___ to use a serif font, but she changed her mind.
explanation: A past plan that changed: was going to + base verb.

sentence: The homepage is effective; ___, the gallery is cluttered.
explanation: After a semicolon, 'however,' links two contrasting sentences.

sentence: ___ its strong colours, the site lacks a clear focal point.
explanation: 'Despite' + a noun phrase (its strong colours). 'Although' needs a full clause.

sentence: The images were compressed ___ the page would load faster.
explanation: 'So that' + a full clause gives the purpose. 'In order to' needs a verb.

sentence: The designer reduced the clutter ___ to make the call to action stand out.
explanation: 'In order to' + base verb gives the purpose.

sentence: The quiz increases engagement, ___ visitors stay on the site longer.
explanation: ', which means that' refers back to the whole idea (singular). 'That' can't follow a comma.

sentence: It could be argued ___ the site is too formal for its audience.
explanation: It could be argued + that + a full clause.

sentence: The asymmetrical layout ___ seem confusing to some visitors.
explanation: 'May' is a modal: no 'to' after it and no -s.

sentence: The site appears ___ aimed at older users.
explanation: appear + to + base verb: appears to be.

sentence: The brief requires the site ___ on mobile phones.
explanation: require + something + to + base verb: requires the site to work.

sentence: The designer suggested ___ the heading font.
explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by the -ing form: suggested changing.

sentence: Visitors are more likely ___ a site that loads quickly.
explanation: be likely + to + base verb.

sentence: The more consistent the design is, ___ credible the site appears.
explanation: The more …, the more …: both halves need 'the'.

sentence: This version is ___ less cluttered than the first iteration.
explanation: Before a comparative (less cluttered), use an adverb: considerably.

sentence: The prompt was too vague, so the AI tool ___ a generic design.
explanation: The story is in the past, so use the past simple: produced.

sentence: My website ___ three pages about our school.
explanation: My website is singular. Use has to say what it includes.

sentence: The buttons ___ blue, green and yellow on screen.
explanation: The buttons is plural, so use are.

sentence: My friend ___ the website name on every page.
explanation: With my friend, add -s to the present simple verb: writes.

sentence: We ___ a short title above the picture.
explanation: After we, use use, without -s, in the present simple.

sentence: There ___ a small picture beside the title.
explanation: A small picture is one thing, so use there is.

sentence: There ___ two buttons below the large picture.
explanation: Two buttons is plural, so use there are.

sentence: On this page, there ___ a short menu.
explanation: A short menu is one thing, so use there is.

sentence: Next to the menu, there ___ three pictures.
explanation: Three pictures is plural, so use there are.

sentence: The menu has four ___ for our class.
explanation: After four, use the plural noun pages.

sentence: I put two ___ beside the school name.
explanation: After two, use the plural noun pictures.

sentence: We use three ___ on the home page.
explanation: After three, use the plural noun colours.

sentence: This page has five ___ under the title.
explanation: After five, use the plural noun buttons.

sentence: You can ___ the menu at the top.
explanation: After can, use the base verb: open.

sentence: We can ___ the words below the picture.
explanation: After can, use the base verb: read.

sentence: I can ___ a new page for you.
explanation: After can, use the base verb: make.

sentence: You can ___ your name in this box.
explanation: After can, use the base verb: type.

sentence: This page does not ___ any large pictures.
explanation: After does not, use the base verb: have.

sentence: We do not ___ yellow for the words.
explanation: After do not, use the base verb: use.

sentence: The menu does not ___ all the pages.
explanation: After does not, use the base verb: show.

sentence: I do not ___ my name on this page.
explanation: After do not, use the base verb: want.

sentence: ___ this website have a page about sport?
explanation: For a present simple question with this website, use Does before have.

sentence: ___ you want a picture beside your name?
explanation: For a present simple question with you, use Do before want.

sentence: ___ these buttons open the other three pages?
explanation: These buttons is plural. Use Do to ask this present simple question.

sentence: ___ the menu show the names of all pages?
explanation: The menu is singular. Use Does before the base verb show.

sentence: My name ___ below the photo of our class.
explanation: My name is singular, so use is.

sentence: The two pictures ___ next to our school logo.
explanation: The two pictures is plural, so use are.

sentence: I ___ happy with the colours on this page.
explanation: Use am with I: I am happy.

sentence: Our class website ___ a very short name.
explanation: Our class website is singular, so use has.

sentence: These pages ___ pictures of all our teachers.
explanation: These pages is plural, so use have.

sentence: ___ is my new website about pet animals.
explanation: Is and website are singular. Use This.

sentence: ___ are the three photos for our home page.
explanation: Are and three photos are plural. Use These.

sentence: The writing on these pages ___ very small.
explanation: The subject is the writing, which is singular. Use is.

sentence: I have a website, and ___ name is Fun Art.
explanation: Use its for the name of a thing such as a website.

sentence: We made this website for ___ school art club.
explanation: Before the noun phrase school art club, use our.

sentence: She puts ___ name at the top of each page.
explanation: Before name, use her: her name.

sentence: He uses ___ photos on the page about animals.
explanation: Before photos, use his: his photos.

sentence: The children put ___ drawings on the class website.
explanation: Before drawings, use their: their drawings.

sentence: You can put ___ email address in this box.
explanation: Before email address, use your.

sentence: This is my website, and I made ___ myself.
explanation: The website is one thing. Use it after made.

sentence: These are our pictures, and we like ___ very much.
explanation: After like, use them for several pictures.

sentence: There is ___ empty box for your name here.
explanation: Empty starts with a vowel sound. Use an before this singular noun phrase.

sentence: We need ___ new picture for the home page.
explanation: Use a before singular new picture. New starts with a consonant sound.

sentence: This website has six ___ about different school clubs.
explanation: After six, use the plural noun pages.

sentence: Our class puts ten ___ in the online gallery.
explanation: After ten, use the plural noun drawings.

sentence: There is only one ___ beside the main picture.
explanation: After one, use the singular noun button.

sentence: The gallery has eight ___ of our school garden.
explanation: After eight, use the plural noun photos.

sentence: We put a ___ under the picture of our teacher.
explanation: A needs a singular noun: a name.

sentence: There are ___ pictures here: one cat and one dog.
explanation: One cat picture and one dog picture make two pictures.

sentence: The school logo is ___ the left of this page.
explanation: We say on the left when describing a position.

sentence: Our names are ___ the bottom of the home page.
explanation: We say at the bottom of a page.

sentence: Please write your name ___ the empty box below.
explanation: Write in a box when you enter information inside it.

sentence: You can click ___ this link to see my work.
explanation: We say click on a link.

sentence: This page is ___ our class and our teachers.
explanation: Use about to say the subject of a page.

sentence: Our new website is ___ children who like drawing.
explanation: Use for to say who the website is intended to help or interest.

sentence: The words are easy ___ read on my phone.
explanation: Use easy to before a base verb: easy to read.

sentence: Click here ___ open the page about our school.
explanation: Use to with a base verb to explain the purpose: to open.

sentence: My sister ___ pictures for the school website every week.
explanation: With my sister, use takes in the present simple.

sentence: Our teacher ___ every new page before we share it.
explanation: With our teacher, use checks in the present simple.

sentence: I ___ the words on every page each morning.
explanation: After I, use check in the present simple.

sentence: The links ___ the other pages on our website.
explanation: The links is plural, so use open.

sentence: This button ___ you to the page about music.
explanation: This button is singular, so use takes.

sentence: The club members ___ their work on this page.
explanation: The club members is plural, so use share.

sentence: Our class ___ a different picture for each page.
explanation: Our class acts as one group here. Use chooses.

sentence: The gallery ___ when you click the blue word.
explanation: The gallery is singular, so use opens.

sentence: You can ___ the picture bigger on your screen.
explanation: After can, use the base verb make.

sentence: We can ___ our drawings on the class website.
explanation: After can, use the base verb share.

sentence: Please ___ your email address in the box below.
explanation: For an instruction after please, use the base verb write.

sentence: Do not ___ the page before saving your work.
explanation: After do not, use the base verb close.

sentence: The pictures ___ not open when I click them.
explanation: Use do not with plural pictures before the base verb open.

sentence: ___ the page easy to read on your phone?
explanation: Use Is to ask whether one page is easy to read.

sentence: The ___ is our club's small name and symbol.
explanation: A logo is a name or symbol used to identify a group.

sentence: The ___ lists Home, About and Contact as page links.
explanation: A menu lists links to different pages or sections.

sentence: The ___ is the big name above this short text.
explanation: A heading names the text or section below it.

sentence: The ___ is the colour behind the words and pictures.
explanation: The background sits behind the other things on a page.

sentence: This ___ is a still picture of our teacher.
explanation: A photo is a still picture taken with a camera.

sentence: The ___ plays a film about our school garden.
explanation: A video shows moving pictures, such as a film.

sentence: The ___ page tells visitors how to email our teacher.
explanation: A Contact page gives visitors ways to get in touch.

sentence: The ___ page tells visitors who we are.
explanation: An About page introduces the people or group behind a website.

sentence: Our ___ puts all twenty class photos together online.
explanation: A gallery displays a collection of pictures.

sentence: The ___ changes how the letters look on this page.
explanation: A font is a particular style of letters.

sentence: Please ___ down to read the rest of the page.
explanation: To scroll is to move through a page that does not all fit on screen.

sentence: Please ___ your name using the letters on your keyboard.
explanation: To type is to enter letters using a keyboard.

sentence: Please ___ your work so you can open it later.
explanation: To save work is to keep a stored copy for later.

sentence: Please ___ the photo you no longer want to keep.
explanation: To delete a photo is to remove it.

sentence: Please ___ the poster to put a paper copy outside.
explanation: To print is to make a paper copy.

sentence: Please ___ the video to see how our club works.
explanation: You watch a video to see its moving pictures.

sentence: The words ___ are the name of the whole website.
explanation: Fun Art names this art website. The other options tell visitors to do something.

sentence: The ___ says 'School News' above the latest stories.
explanation: A heading names the section below it.

sentence: The ___ has boxes for your name and message.
explanation: A form has fields where visitors enter information.

sentence: Use the ___ page to return to the site's main page.
explanation: Home is the website's main page.

sentence: The ___ is a set of connected pages online.
explanation: A website is a collection of connected web pages.

sentence: The ___ is under the photo and describes it.
explanation: A caption is text that explains a picture.

sentence: The ___ menu opens a list of links below it.
explanation: A dropdown menu opens a list below its label.

sentence: The ___ gives the school's address in written words.
explanation: Written information such as an address is text.

sentence: The ___ shows a different picture when the film plays.
explanation: A screen displays the moving pictures in a film.

sentence: Click ___ to hear the song on this page.
explanation: The Play control starts audio or video.

sentence: Click ___ to stop the film for a moment.
explanation: Pause stops playback temporarily so you can continue later.

sentence: The ___ lets you hear the teacher's recorded voice.
explanation: An audio player plays recorded sound.

sentence: Click ___ to send the finished form to our teacher.
explanation: Submit sends the information entered in a form.

sentence: Click ___ to make another copy of this picture.
explanation: Copy makes another version of the selected item.

sentence: Of all twelve pictures in the gallery, this one is the ___.
explanation: A comparison with all twelve pictures needs the superlative form largest.

sentence: The new buttons are ___ than the old ones, so they are easier to tap.
explanation: Before than, use the comparative form larger.

sentence: The text is not big ___ to read without moving closer to the screen.
explanation: Put enough after the adjective: big enough to read.

sentence: The page is ___ wide to fit on my phone without moving it sideways.
explanation: Use too before an adjective when something goes beyond a useful limit.

sentence: The new website looks ___, with clear labels and a simple menu.
explanation: After looks, use the adjective professional to describe the website.

sentence: Yesterday, our teacher ___ us how to add a link to the class website.
explanation: Yesterday places the action in the past, so use showed.

sentence: We are going ___ a page about our school garden next week.
explanation: Use going to followed by the base verb: going to add.

sentence: I did not ___ the old photos because we still need them.
explanation: After did not, use the base verb delete.

sentence: ___ you change the home page after our lesson yesterday?
explanation: Yesterday needs a past simple question: Did you change it?

sentence: Look at the screen: the designer is ___ a picture into the gallery.
explanation: After is, use moving for an action happening now.

sentence: Right now, the students ___ checking whether the buttons work on their phones.
explanation: The students is plural. Use are before checking.

sentence: The new page does not have ___ videos, but it has several photos.
explanation: Use any before a plural noun in this negative statement.

sentence: There is too ___ information in this small box, so the words look crowded.
explanation: Information is uncountable, so use much.

sentence: How ___ pages does the website have, including the home page?
explanation: Pages is countable and plural. Ask how many.

sentence: The instructions are ___ written, so visitors can follow each step.
explanation: Use the adverb clearly to describe how the instructions are written.

sentence: You can download the club timetable ___ our website and keep it on your phone.
explanation: Use from to name the place where a download comes from.

sentence: The two students made a website, and this is ___ final design.
explanation: Before final design, use their.

sentence: We put ___ useful map on the Contact page to help visitors find the school.
explanation: Useful begins with a consonant sound, like you. Use a.

sentence: You should ___ the links before you share the finished website with your class.
explanation: After should, use the base verb test.

sentence: This page ___ not need a video because the photographs explain everything.
explanation: For singular this page, use does not before need.

sentence: The list of club activities ___ below the large photograph on the home page.
explanation: The subject is the list, which is singular. Use is.

sentence: Last night, I ___ the wrong picture, so I added the correct one this morning.
explanation: Last night needs the past simple form uploaded.

sentence: The new menu makes it easier ___ the page about school clubs.
explanation: Use easier to followed by a base verb: easier to find.

sentence: Visitors click the small picture ___ see a larger copy of the same image.
explanation: Use to with a base verb to explain the purpose: to see.

sentence: The ___ at the bottom of every page contains the copyright notice and useful links.
explanation: A footer is the section at the bottom of a page.

sentence: The ___ at the top of every page contains the school logo and main menu.
explanation: A header is the top section of a page, often containing the logo and menu.

sentence: Visitors type a word into the ___ to find matching pages on the website.
explanation: A search box accepts words used to find matching content.

sentence: The ___ asks for your name, email address and message before you click Send.
explanation: A contact form collects information so visitors can send a message.

sentence: Clicking the ___ reveals a list of smaller page links underneath its label.
explanation: A dropdown menu opens a list below its label.

sentence: The ___ beneath the photograph names the students and explains what they are doing.
explanation: A caption explains a particular picture, often from below it.

sentence: The ___ displays all our paintings together, with each picture opening when you click it.
explanation: A gallery is a collection of images displayed together.

sentence: The ___ page introduces our club leaders and explains why we started the club.
explanation: An About page explains who runs a group and what it does.

sentence: The ___ page gives the school address, telephone number and a way to send a message.
explanation: A Contact page gives visitors ways to get in touch.

sentence: The ___ is a smaller copy of a photo that you can click to enlarge.
explanation: A thumbnail is a small image used to preview a larger one.

sentence: To save the website's poster as a file on your computer, choose ___.
explanation: Download transfers a file from a website to your device.

sentence: To send a photo from your computer to the website's gallery, choose ___.
explanation: Upload transfers a file from your device to an online service.

sentence: When you click ___, the browser loads the current page again to show any changes.
explanation: Refresh loads the current page again.

sentence: The ___ lets you move down a long page by dragging its handle beside the content.
explanation: A scrollbar lets you move through content that extends beyond the visible area.

sentence: The designer changes the ___ from grey to white without changing the text colour.
explanation: The background is the colour or image behind the page's content.

sentence: The designer changes the ___ so that every letter has a different style.
explanation: Changing the font changes the design of the letters.

sentence: The menu links are too small, so the designer makes the text size ___.
explanation: Larger text gives small menu labels more space and makes them easier to see.

sentence: The page contains too many pictures in a small area, so it looks ___.
explanation: Crowded describes many things packed into too little space.

sentence: The ___ called 'School Life' tells readers the subject of the section below it.
explanation: A heading names a section of writing.

sentence: Visitors enter their email address in a ___ so the club can send them weekly news.
explanation: A text field is a box where visitors type information.

sentence: The ___ contains the written words of an article, rather than its pictures or video.
explanation: Body text is the main written content, separate from headings.

sentence: The ___ explains the first step, the second step and the third step in numbered order.
explanation: A numbered list presents items in an ordered sequence.

sentence: The ___ groups short points using dots at the start of each line.
explanation: A bullet list uses marks such as dots to separate points.

sentence: The ___ shows the same school symbol on every page so visitors recognise the website.
explanation: A repeated logo helps visitors recognise the organisation behind a site.

sentence: The site's ___ tells the browser where to find it, such as the address you type at the top.
explanation: A web address identifies the online location of a site or page.

sentence: The row of links to the site's main sections stays across the top of each page, forming the ___.
explanation: A navigation bar groups links to the main pages or sections of a website.

sentence: After reading to the end of the page, visitors find the copyright notice and legal links in the ___.
explanation: The footer is the bottom section of a page, often containing legal information and useful links.

sentence: Below the navigation, a large photograph and a short introduction fill the first main section, known as the ___.
explanation: The hero section is a prominent opening section that introduces the page's main message.

sentence: The bright 'Book a visit' button is the page's ___ because it asks visitors to take a specific next step.
explanation: A call to action encourages a specific action, such as making a booking.

sentence: The small 'Home > Clubs > Music' links show where this page sits within the site and are called ___.
explanation: Breadcrumbs show a page's position within the website's structure.

sentence: Related articles appear in a narrow column beside the main story, so this extra content is placed in the ___.
explanation: A sidebar is a column beside the main content, often containing related information or links.

sentence: Instead of opening every section, visitors type 'chess club' into the ___ to find pages containing those words.
explanation: A search bar lets visitors find content using words they enter.

sentence: Selecting 'Clubs' opens a list of links directly below the label, so this navigation control is a ___.
explanation: A dropdown menu reveals a list below its label.

sentence: On the mobile version, three horizontal lines open the main navigation when tapped, creating the familiar ___.
explanation: A hamburger menu uses a three-line icon to open navigation, often on smaller screens.

sentence: The art page displays a collection of student paintings that visitors can browse together, so its main feature is a ___.
explanation: A gallery presents a collection of images for visitors to browse.

sentence: To keep the gallery compact, each full-size photograph is represented by a small preview image called a ___.
explanation: A thumbnail is a small preview of a larger image.

sentence: The sentence directly beneath the photograph identifies the students and describes the event, making it the image's ___.
explanation: A caption is visible text associated with a picture that explains or identifies it.

sentence: The image's description is read aloud by a screen reader when the photograph cannot be seen, so it is ___.
explanation: Alt text provides a text alternative for an image, including for people using screen readers.

sentence: When the pointer rests on the unfamiliar icon, a small explanatory label appears beside it as a ___.
explanation: A tooltip gives a short explanation when a user points at or focuses on an element.

sentence: The underlined words 'View timetable' open another page when selected, so the words act as a ___.
explanation: A hyperlink connects the selected text or element to another destination.

sentence: Visitors keep asking the same questions about joining, so the designer groups the common questions and answers in the ___.
explanation: An FAQ section answers frequently asked questions.

sentence: To explain who founded the club and what its members hope to achieve, the designer adds an ___.
explanation: An About page introduces the organisation, its people and its purpose.

sentence: The school's address, telephone number and message form belong together on the ___ so visitors can get in touch.
explanation: A Contact page brings together ways to reach the organisation.

sentence: The student publishes dated articles about each stage of her project, with the newest first, using a ___.
explanation: A blog presents posts or articles, commonly ordered with the most recent first.

sentence: Rather than displaying every classroom exercise, the designer selects her strongest finished projects to present in her ___.
explanation: A portfolio is a selected collection of work used to show skills and achievements.

sentence: The quoted comment from a satisfied workshop visitor appears with their name and describes their experience, making it a ___.
explanation: A testimonial is a person's account of their experience, often used to build trust.

sentence: Visitors enter their email address to receive future club updates, so the boxes and Subscribe button form a ___.
explanation: A newsletter form collects details from people who want regular updates.

sentence: Visitors may choose several interests at once, so the form uses square controls that can be ticked independently, called ___.
explanation: Checkboxes allow independent selections, so several options can be chosen together.

sentence: Visitors must choose exactly one delivery method from a visible group of circular controls, so the form uses ___.
explanation: A group of radio buttons allows one option to be selected at a time.

sentence: When visitors type their secret login code, the characters are hidden by dots inside the ___.
explanation: A password field masks the characters a user enters.

sentence: The form needs space for a message across several lines, so the designer includes a ___ rather than a single-line box.
explanation: A text area accepts longer messages across multiple lines.

sentence: The pale example address inside the email box disappears when typing begins, so it is ___ rather than a permanent label.
explanation: Placeholder text appears inside an empty field and usually disappears when the user enters a value.

sentence: The words 'Email address' remain above the box after the visitor starts typing, so they are its ___.
explanation: A field label identifies what information belongs in a field and can remain visible during typing.

sentence: As the file uploads, a horizontal indicator gradually fills from zero to one hundred per cent, acting as a ___.
explanation: A progress bar shows how much of a task has been completed.

sentence: The article list is divided into numbered pages with Next and Previous controls, so the designer has added ___.
explanation: Pagination divides a long collection into separate pages that users can move between.

sentence: The opening image display rotates through three photographs, with arrows for moving between them, so it is a ___.
explanation: A carousel displays a sequence of slides or images within the same space.

sentence: Each question expands to reveal its answer beneath it when selected, so the FAQ uses an ___ to save space.
explanation: An accordion lets users expand and collapse sections of content.

sentence: Selecting 'Overview', 'Prices' or 'Dates' changes the content in the same panel, so these controls work as ___.
explanation: Tabs switch between related content panels while keeping the controls visible.

sentence: The page is dimmed while a confirmation window appears above it and requires a response, so the window is a ___.
explanation: A modal dialog requires the user to deal with it before returning to the underlying page.

sentence: The notice asks visitors whether to allow optional tracking files and provides Accept and Reject buttons, making it a ___.
explanation: A cookie banner can present information and choices about a site's use of cookies.

sentence: An old link leads to a message explaining that the requested page cannot be found, so visitors see an ___.
explanation: An error page explains a problem such as a missing page and can offer a way to continue.

sentence: The small school symbol beside the website's name in the browser tab is its ___, helping visitors recognise the open tab.
explanation: A favicon is the small site icon commonly shown in a browser tab.

sentence: To help visitors browse the site's overall structure, the designer creates a ___ listing its pages in organised groups.
explanation: A visitor-facing sitemap provides an organised overview of links to the site's pages.

sentence: Before choosing colours or photographs, the designer draws a simple plan of boxes showing where content will go, called a ___.
explanation: A wireframe plans page structure and content positions before detailed visual design.

sentence: The team tests a clickable model of the planned website before the real site is built, so they use a ___.
explanation: A prototype models how a design will work and can let people try interactions.

sentence: The photographs line up in repeated rows and columns, giving the gallery a clear ___ that keeps the layout organised.
explanation: A grid organises content using repeated rows and columns.

sentence: The designer leaves empty space around the heading instead of adding more pictures, using ___ to separate it from nearby content.
explanation: Whitespace is empty space around or between elements. It does not have to be white.

sentence: Dark text against a pale background is easier to distinguish than pale text on white because it has stronger ___.
explanation: Contrast is the difference between elements, such as light and dark colours.

sentence: The title is largest, section headings are smaller and body text is smallest, creating a clear ___ for readers.
explanation: Visual hierarchy uses differences such as size to show the relative importance of information.

sentence: The designer uses the same chosen set of blue, cream and grey shades throughout the site, keeping its ___ consistent.
explanation: A colour palette is the set of colours selected for a design.

sentence: The three-column layout becomes a single column on phones, so the site uses ___ to suit different screen sizes.
explanation: Responsive design adapts a layout to different screen sizes.

sentence: The button changes colour only while the pointer rests on it, so the designer has created a visible ___.
explanation: A hover state shows how an element looks while a pointer is over it.

sentence: All paragraph edges begin on the same vertical line, so the designer has improved the text's ___.
explanation: Alignment places elements along shared lines or edges.

sentence: Because the site is designed mainly for younger children, those children are its ___ and should guide the language choices.
explanation: The target audience is the group a website is intended to reach.

sentence: The club's recognisable symbol appears beside its name on every page, so the designer has repeated the ___ for consistency.
explanation: A logo is a symbol or design used to identify an organisation or brand.

sentence: Although the article continues for several screens, the navigation remains attached to the upper edge after visitors scroll past its original position, behaving as a ___.
explanation: A sticky header can stay at the top of the screen after reaching that position during scrolling.

sentence: Rather than opening a different page, the 'See prices' control moves the visitor directly to the pricing section further down the current page, using an ___.
explanation: An anchor link can jump to a named section within the same page.

sentence: Because visitors can enter through a detailed article without seeing the home page, the designer adds ___ showing the article's parent sections and its place in the site.
explanation: Breadcrumbs show a page's position within a site's hierarchy and link to its parent sections.

sentence: After selecting 'Photography', visitors see only photography projects while the other categories disappear from the results, showing that the category control acts as a ___.
explanation: A filter restricts the results to items that meet a condition. Sorting changes their order instead.

sentence: When visitors choose 'Newest first', every project remains available but the sequence changes according to date, so they have used the ___.
explanation: A sort control changes the order of results without excluding items simply because they are older.

sentence: Instead of loading every article into one continuous list, the site divides results into separate numbered screens and supplies Next and Previous links, using ___.
explanation: Pagination splits a collection into pages that users can navigate between.

sentence: Since most visitors need only one answer, each FAQ question opens its own answer immediately underneath, while the other questions remain available in an ___.
explanation: An accordion reveals or hides content beneath section headings, so visitors can open the answers they need.

sentence: The labels 'Description', 'Dates' and 'Prices' remain visible while selecting one replaces the content of a shared panel, so the product information is organised into ___.
explanation: Tabs switch between associated panels. The controls remain available while the selected panel changes.

sentence: Before deleting a project, visitors must respond to a confirmation window that prevents interaction with the dimmed page behind it, making this window a ___.
explanation: A modal dialog temporarily blocks interaction with the underlying page until it is dealt with.

sentence: To explain an unfamiliar symbol without adding permanent text beside it, the designer makes a brief label appear when the icon receives hover or focus, using a ___.
explanation: A tooltip gives brief supporting information associated with an element on hover or focus.

sentence: When a visitor presses Tab, a clear outline moves between links and buttons, revealing which control will respond to the keyboard through a visible ___.
explanation: A focus indicator identifies the element currently selected for keyboard interaction. Hover refers to a pointer being over something.

sentence: To prevent keyboard users from moving through the same long menu on every visit, the designer adds a ___ that jumps directly to the main content.
explanation: A skip link lets users bypass repeated content such as navigation and move to the main section.

sentence: Because the photograph communicates information that cannot be understood from the surrounding article alone, the designer provides a meaningful text alternative in its ___.
explanation: Alt text supplies an image's relevant information or purpose as a text alternative.

sentence: The interview's spoken words appear as text timed to the video, together with relevant sound information, so viewers can follow it without hearing through the ___.
explanation: Video captions present speech and relevant sounds in text synchronised with playback.

sentence: Visitors who prefer reading can open a separate written record of the interview from beginning to end, rather than following timed text over the video, using a ___.
explanation: A transcript gives a written version of recorded speech and can include relevant sound information.

sentence: The instruction inside the empty box vanishes as soon as typing begins, so the designer adds a permanent ___ above it to identify the required information.
explanation: A persistent field label identifies a field even after its placeholder disappears.

sentence: When a visitor enters letters into a field that requires a number, the site identifies the affected box and explains the problem through ___.
explanation: Form validation checks entered information against requirements and can explain how to correct it.

sentence: After the form is successfully submitted, a short notice confirms that the message was received and explains the expected response time, acting as a ___.
explanation: A confirmation message tells visitors that an action succeeded and can explain what happens next.

sentence: The Submit button cannot be activated until the required agreement is selected, so its inactive appearance communicates a ___ rather than a temporary loading process.
explanation: A disabled state shows that a control is currently unavailable. A loading state shows a task already in progress.

sentence: While the site retrieves a large gallery, an animated symbol tells visitors that processing is still happening, although no completion percentage is available, serving as a ___.
explanation: A loading indicator shows that work is underway. It does not have to show a measurable percentage.

sentence: A newly created portfolio has no projects yet, so the page explains the absence and offers an Add project button as part of its ___.
explanation: An empty state explains why a view currently has no content and can suggest a useful next action.

sentence: Although the content remains the same, its columns rearrange automatically to fit the available screen width without requiring sideways scrolling, demonstrating a ___.
explanation: A responsive layout adapts the arrangement of content to the available screen space.

sentence: At a chosen screen width, the three-column gallery switches to one column and the navigation changes form, so that width is a design ___.
explanation: A breakpoint is a chosen width at which responsive layout rules change.

sentence: The designer increases the space outside the card's border so neighbouring cards move farther away, while the content inside the card stays unchanged, adjusting its ___.
explanation: A margin is space outside an element's border. Padding is space between the border and its content.

sentence: Because the paragraph sits too close to the inside edge of its bordered box, the designer increases the box's ___ without changing the paragraph's words.
explanation: Padding adds space between an element's content and its border. A margin is outside the border.

sentence: Rather than filling every available gap with decoration, the designer leaves deliberate empty areas around related content, using ___ to improve separation and reduce crowding.
explanation: Whitespace is the unoccupied space around and between elements, regardless of the background colour.

sentence: Although individual photographs have different subjects, their edges follow the same underlying system of rows and columns, giving the page a consistent ___.
explanation: A grid structure organises elements using shared rows and columns, helping their positions remain consistent.

sentence: By varying size, weight and position, the designer makes the booking information noticeable before supporting details, establishing a ___ that guides the order of attention.
explanation: A visual hierarchy makes some information more prominent than other information, guiding what people notice first.

sentence: The text size remains unchanged, but replacing pale grey letters with dark blue makes them easier to distinguish from the white background by increasing ___.
explanation: Contrast concerns differences such as lightness between text and its background. The change does not alter text size or spacing.

sentence: Although the heading explains the workshop, the prominent 'Reserve your place' button turns that information into an explicit invitation to act, functioning as the main ___.
explanation: A call to action asks visitors to take a specific step. Here, that step is reserving a place.

sentence: The page prioritises booking, but a quieter 'View the programme' link offers an alternative for visitors who need more information, serving as a ___.
explanation: A secondary action offers an alternative next step while the main action remains more prominent.

sentence: Rather than treating the logo and navigation as the main introduction, the designer uses the large opening image, headline and booking button below them as the ___.
explanation: The hero section is a prominent opening block that introduces the main message and can include an action button.

sentence: The copyright details and legal links repeat beneath the main content on every page, so they belong in the ___ rather than the opening promotional section.
explanation: The footer is the recurring section at the bottom of a page, often used for legal and supporting links.

sentence: To keep the article itself uninterrupted, the designer places related links in a separate narrow column running alongside the text, creating a ___.
explanation: A sidebar holds supporting content in a column beside the main page content.

sentence: Before selecting photographs or typefaces, the team sketches boxes to agree where the main sections should sit, using a ___ to discuss structure rather than appearance.
explanation: A wireframe is a simplified structural plan showing content positions before detailed styling.

sentence: The client needs to approve the proposed colours, fonts and imagery, so the designer presents a detailed static visual design, commonly called a ___.
explanation: A mockup shows the proposed visual appearance. It can be static without working interactions.

sentence: Because the team needs to test whether visitors can move from an event listing to a booking screen, it creates a clickable ___ before building the finished site.
explanation: A clickable prototype models interactions and movement between screens before the final site is built.

sentence: Rather than asking only whether the colours look attractive, the designer observes visitors trying to find a timetable without help, carrying out a ___.
explanation: A usability test observes how people complete tasks and identifies difficulties in using the design.

sentence: Visitors expect workshop dates under Events, but the current site hides them under About, so the designer revises the grouping and labelling of content within its ___.
explanation: Information architecture concerns how content is organised, grouped and labelled so people can find it.

sentence: Although the articles change each week, the logo, colours and typography remain recognisable across every page, maintaining a consistent ___ for the organisation.
explanation: A visual identity is the recognisable visual style created through elements such as logos, colours and typography.

sentence: The site replaces formal instructions with friendly, direct sentences while keeping its colours and layout unchanged, so the main revision concerns its ___.
explanation: Tone of voice describes how writing sounds to its audience, including its degree of formality.

sentence: Because several equally bright elements compete for attention, the designer makes one image clearly dominant so the page has an identifiable ___ for the viewer.
explanation: A focal point is the element or area that draws the strongest attention.

sentence: When the designer changes an image's width and height in different proportions, faces look stretched, showing that the image's original ___ has not been preserved.
explanation: The aspect ratio is the relationship between an image's width and height. Changing it can distort the image.

sentence: The photographs keep the same visible dimensions, but their files become smaller so they transfer more quickly, showing that the designer has used ___.
explanation: Image compression reduces file size. It can do this without changing the image's pixel dimensions.

sentence: To remove a distracting object near the edge while keeping the subject, the designer cuts away part of the photograph instead of stretching it, using ___.
explanation: Cropping removes outer parts of an image to change what remains visible.

sentence: Although the main menu contains only the most important sections, a separate page provides an organised collection of links to pages throughout the site, forming a ___.
explanation: A visitor-facing sitemap provides an organised overview of links across a site.

sentence: The 'Our team' link opens another page on the same website, rather than sending visitors to a different website, so it is an ___.
explanation: An internal link connects pages or locations within the same website.

sentence: Before visitors send personal details through the contact form, a linked notice explains why the information is collected and how it will be used, providing a ___.
explanation: A privacy notice explains how an organisation collects and uses personal information.

sentence: Although the telephone number is optional, the form refuses submission without an email address, showing that the email box has been set as a ___.
explanation: A required field must contain the requested information before a form can be submitted.
